---
title: "Indicator: Life expectancy at birth, British Columbia"
---

*Status: second published indicator (milestone M3 in progress). Regenerate
with `uv run sohbc build life_expectancy_bc`.*

This indicator is fetched from a catalogued Statistics Canada table,
tidied by the same pipeline as the
[mortality indicator](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd), and published as
a versioned dataset plus the views below. Each indicator page states its
provenance and caveats (see the [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md), milestone M3).

## Provenance

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Domain** | [Mortality](../reference/measurement-framework.qmd) |
| **Definition** | Life expectancy at birth (age 0), in years, by sex (both sexes, males, females), resident in British Columbia, from the complete life table [@statcan_life_table] |
| **Source** | Statistics Canada, table 13-10-0837-01, *Life expectancy and other elements of the complete life table, single-year estimates, Canada, all provinces except Prince Edward Island* [@statcan_life_table] |
| **Access** | Statistics Canada Web Data Service (automated full-table download) |
| **Form** | indicator table (published summary statistics) |
| **Geography** | British Columbia (no sub-provincial rows in this table) |
| **Coverage** | 1980–2024 (annual, single-year estimates); observation window shown on each figure |
| **Frequency / refresh** | annual |
| **Licence** | Statistics Canada Open Licence |
| **Proxy note** | A proxy for the mortality domain, not the state of health itself ([why](../explanation/definition-of-health.qmd#proxies-are-not-the-state-of-health)) |

## Trend

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows = FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
e0 = rows.filter(d => d.characteristic === "Life expectancy (in years) at age x (ex)" && d.age_group === "0 years")
bySex = e0.filter(d => d.sex !== "Both sexes")
headline = e0.filter(d => d.sex === "Both sexes")
trend = FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc_trend.json").json()
bySexTrend = FileAttachment("../data/published/life_expectancy_bc_by_sex_trend.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  title: "Life expectancy at birth, British Columbia (years)",
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {grid: true, label: "Years", domain: [70, 90]},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectX([{x1: 2020, x2: 2024}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "grey", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
    Plot.ruleX(bySexTrend.levels.Males.change_points, {stroke: "red", strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
    Plot.ruleX(bySexTrend.levels.Females.change_points, {stroke: "steelblue", strokeDasharray: "2,3"}),
    Plot.lineY(bySex, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(bySex, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

The grey band marks the COVID-19 period (2020–2024); the red dashed lines
are the male series' regime breaks, the blue dotted lines the female
series'. Life expectancy is a **period** measure: it is the average length
of life a synthetic cohort would experience if it lived its whole life
under the age-specific death rates of that year [@statcan_life_table].

## Trajectory and regimes

Trend summaries, recomputed on every build
(`data/published/life_expectancy_bc_trend.json`,
`data/published/life_expectancy_bc_by_sex_trend.json`):

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Over ${trend.start}–${trend.end} life expectancy at birth (both sexes)
changed by **${trend.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** years per
decade, and the series is **${trend.stationarity.verdict}**. It carries a
monotone trend (Kendall's tau = ${trend.trend_test.tau.toFixed(2)},
p = ${trend.trend_test.p_value.toFixed(3)}) and departure from a single
straight line (residual-permutation test,
p = ${trend.break_test.p_value.toFixed(3)}). The BIC-selected regimes
break at ${trend.change_points.join(", ")}.`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sexRows = ["Males", "Females"].map(sex => ({
  sex,
  ...bySexTrend.levels[sex]
})).map(d => ({
  sex: d.sex,
  start: d.start,
  end: d.end,
  slope_per_decade: d.overall.slope_per_decade,
  verdict: d.stationarity.verdict,
  change_points: d.change_points.join(", ") || "—",
  change_point: d.change_point ?? "—"
}))
Inputs.table(sexRows, {
  columns: ["sex", "start", "end", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "change_points", "change_point"],
  header: {sex: "sex", start: "from", end: "to", slope_per_decade: "slope/decade", verdict: "stationarity", change_points: "regime breaks", change_point: "largest break"}
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Both sex-specific series are **${bySexTrend.levels.Males.stationarity.verdict}** over
${bySexTrend.levels.Males.start}–${bySexTrend.levels.Males.end}. Females
live longer than males at every observed year, and the female advantage is
roughly constant in levels though not in the dating of its regimes. The
period includes the COVID-19 mortality shock, visible as the 2020–2022
dip; the pipeline dates it and does not attribute it.`
```

**Method.** Regimes are dated by a piecewise-linear segmentation, solved
exactly by dynamic programming, with the number of breaks chosen by BIC;
whether the series departs from one straight line is tested by residual
permutation [@truong2020selective], and the trend by Kendall's tau. Each
series is therefore labelled stationary or not over its observed window,
as milestone M3 requires. The full test output, including every candidate
segmentation, is in the trend JSON. The permutation test assumes
exchangeable residuals — autocorrelation is not modelled — so it is a
test of departure from a linear trend, not a full time-series model.

## Caveats

- **Period, not cohort.** Life expectancy at birth is a period life-table
  quantity: it is not the expected lifespan of anyone actually born in
  that year, and it says nothing about the health of the living
  [@statcan_life_table].
- **Break detection, not explanation.** The regimes are dated by a formal
  test (above); the test says a break beyond a single straight line
  exists, not what caused it. Recent-year estimates rest on few data
  points and are the least certain.
- **Sex categories are the source's.** The table publishes both sexes,
  males, and females; the pipeline reports these as given.
- **Coverage.** The source series is 1980–2024 and excludes Prince Edward
  Island from the published table; the BC series itself is complete. This
  table has **no sub-provincial rows** — health-authority and regional
  life tables are separate Statistics Canada products.
- **Revisions.** Statistics Canada may revise recent-year estimates; the
  published files are regenerated from the source on each build.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run sohbc fetch statcan_life_tables
uv run sohbc build life_expectancy_bc
```

The tidy dataset is published at `data/published/life_expectancy_bc.csv`
(all ages and elements, by sex). The headline trend tests are at
`data/published/life_expectancy_bc_trend.json` and the per-sex tests at
`data/published/life_expectancy_bc_by_sex_trend.json`.
